title: Grateful Dead Live at Gaelic Park on 1971-08-26
source: AKG190E > Uher 400L, taped by Marty Weinberg and unknown aud

ai_review.summary: Decent outdoor audience tape with uneven sound but a spacey “Other One” that captures the raunchy early‑70s Dead vibe.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience capture from Gaelic Park, offering a generally listenable mix though the sound is uneven and vocals can be hot. Musically the show is typical of the brief early‑70s period – loose and raunchy – with a standout, space‑filled “Other One” and a memorable scream into “Not Fade Away.” Overall it’s an enjoyable snapshot for fans who aren’t strict soundboard purists.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers gave 3‑star ratings, noting decent but uneven audio and an average performance with a few highlights; the consistent moderate feedback yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound is uneven throughout with hot vocals at times; Jerry's guitar cuts through loudly and clearly, while overall ambience is typical of outdoor audience tapes from the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑70s Dead set – loose, raunchy and a bit sloppy, but with energetic moments that keep the flow lively.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar is loud and clear; praised for cutting through the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Sings the Northbound Train verse during "Rider"; vocals noted as hot at times.
